title: Transition to the ContainerLogV2 table by 30 September 2026
summary: You're receiving this notification because you are associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor container insights.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you are associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor container insights. On 30 September 2026, we'll retire the ContainerLog table in Azure Monitor and you'll need to transition to the ContainerLogV2 table. The ContainerLogV2 table offers all the functionality of ContainerLog, plus: Compatibility with the basic logs pricing tier. Additional pod and container metadata for easier querying. Support for multiline log entries. Recommended action To ensure your alerts and dashboards continue to work as expected, transition (https://aka.ms/containerlogmigration) to ContainerLogV2 by 30 September 2026. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://aka.ms/ContainerLogQA). If you have a support plan and need technical help, open the Azure portal (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/overview) and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.
recommended_actions: To ensure your alerts and dashboards continue to work as expected, transition (https://aka.ms/containerlogmigration) to ContainerLogV2 by 30 September 2026.

title: Azure Monitor Action Groups: Email OTP Verification for Enhanced Security
summary: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor Action Groups.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor Action Groups. Azure Monitor Action Groups has officially rolled out the new OTP feature to all regions in the Public cloud. New email addresses added to new or existing action groups must be verified using a one-time passcode (OTP) before they can receive notifications. This change is aimed at improving overall security. No immediate action is required for email addresses that are already configured in existing action groups. These addresses will continue to receive notifications. These addresses will be marked as "Legacy Allowed" after the rollout. However, adding a legacy-allowed email address to a new action group will require OTP verification. All new email addresses must complete a one-time verification within the same tenant before receiving notifications. An OTP email will be sent when the action group is saved, and the passcode will expire after 30 minutes. If needed, a new verification email can be requested from the Azure Portal Action Group blade. As part of this change, users will also be required to save and verify an email address before they are able to send test email notifications. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://aka.ms/azureqa). If you have a support plan and need technical help, create a support request. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request)

title: Azure Monitor Action Groups: Email OTP Verification for Enhanced Security
summary: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor Action Groups.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor Action Groups. Azure Monitor Action Groups has officially rolled out the new OTP feature to all regions in the Public cloud. New email addresses added to new or existing action groups must be verified using a one-time passcode (OTP) before they can receive notifications. This change is aimed at improving overall security. No immediate action is required for email addresses that are already configured in existing action groups. These addresses will continue to receive notifications. These addresses will be marked as "Legacy Allowed" after the rollout. However, adding a legacy-allowed email address to a new action group will require OTP verification. All new email addresses must complete a one-time verification within the same tenant before receiving notifications. An OTP email will be sent when the action group is saved, and the passcode will expire after 30 minutes. If needed, a new verification email can be requested from the Azure Portal Action Group blade. As part of this change, users will also be required to save and verify an email address before they are able to send test email notifications. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://aka.ms/azureqa). If you have a support plan and need technical help, create a support request. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request)

description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor Action Groups. Azure Monitor Action Groups has officially rolled out the new OTP feature to all regions in the Public cloud. New email addresses added to new or existing action groups must be verified using a one-time passcode (OTP) before they can receive notifications. This change is aimed at improving overall security. No immediate action is required for email addresses that are already configured in existing action groups. These addresses will continue to receive notifications. These addresses will be marked as "Legacy Allowed" after the rollout. However, adding a legacy-allowed email address to a new action group will require OTP verification. All new email addresses must complete a one-time verification within the same tenant before receiving notifications. An OTP email will be sent when the action group is saved, and the passcode will expire after 30 minutes. If needed, a new verification email can be requested from the Azure Portal Action Group blade. As part of this change, users will also be required to save and verify an email address before they are able to send test email notifications. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://aka.ms/azureqa). If you have a support plan and need technical help, create a support request. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request)

summary: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor Action Groups.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor Action Groups. Azure Monitor Action Groups has officially rolled out the new OTP feature to all regions in the Public cloud. New email addresses added to new or existing action groups must be verified using a one-time passcode (OTP) before they can receive notifications. This change is aimed at improving overall security. No immediate action is required for email addresses that are already configured in existing action groups. These addresses will continue to receive notifications. These addresses will be marked as "Legacy Allowed" after the rollout. However, adding a legacy-allowed email address to a new action group will require OTP verification. All new email addresses must complete a one-time verification within the same tenant before receiving notifications. An OTP email will be sent when the action group is saved, and the passcode will expire after 30 minutes. If needed, a new verification email can be requested from the Azure Portal Action Group blade. As part of this change, users will also be required to save and verify an email address before they are able to send test email notifications. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://aka.ms/azureqa). If you have a support plan and need technical help, create a support request. title: Azure Monitor Action Groups: Email OTP Verification for Enhanced Security
summary: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor Action Groups.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor Action Groups. Azure Monitor Action Groups has officially rolled out the new OTP feature to all regions in the Public cloud. New email addresses added to new or existing action groups must be verified using a one-time passcode (OTP) before they can receive notifications. This change is aimed at improving overall security. No immediate action is required for email addresses that are already configured in existing action groups. These addresses will continue to receive notifications. These addresses will be marked as "Legacy Allowed" after the rollout. However, adding a legacy-allowed email address to a new action group will require OTP verification. All new email addresses must complete a one-time verification within the same tenant before receiving notifications. An OTP email will be sent when the action group is saved, and the passcode will expire after 30 minutes. If needed, a new verification email can be requested from the Azure Portal Action Group blade. As part of this change, users will also be required to save and verify an email address before they are able to send test email notifications. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://aka.ms/azureqa). If you have a support plan and need technical help, create a support request. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request)

title: Transition to the ContainerLogV2 table by 30 September 2026
summary: You're receiving this notification because you are associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor container insights.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you are associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor container insights. On 30 September 2026, we'll retire the ContainerLog table in Azure Monitor and you'll need to transition to the ContainerLogV2 table. The ContainerLogV2 table offers all the functionality of ContainerLog, plus: Compatibility with the basic logs pricing tier. Additional pod and container metadata for easier querying. Support for multiline log entries. Recommended action To ensure your alerts and dashboards continue to work as expected, transition (https://aka.ms/containerlogmigration) to ContainerLogV2 by 30 September 2026. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://aka.ms/ContainerLogQA). If you have a support plan and need technical help, open the Azure portal (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/overview) and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.
recommended_actions: To ensure your alerts and dashboards continue to work as expected, transition (https://aka.ms/containerlogmigration) to ContainerLogV2 by 30 September 2026.

title: Azure Monitor Action Groups: Email OTP Verification for Enhanced Security
summary: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor Action Groups.
description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor Action Groups. Azure Monitor Action Groups has officially rolled out the new OTP feature to all regions in the Public cloud. New email addresses added to new or existing action groups must be verified using a one-time passcode (OTP) before they can receive notifications. This change is aimed at improving overall security. No immediate action is required for email addresses that are already configured in existing action groups. These addresses will continue to receive notifications. These addresses will be marked as "Legacy Allowed" after the rollout. However, adding a legacy-allowed email address to a new action group will require OTP verification. All new email addresses must complete a one-time verification within the same tenant before receiving notifications. An OTP email will be sent when the action group is saved, and the passcode will expire after 30 minutes. If needed, a new verification email can be requested from the Azure Portal Action Group blade. As part of this change, users will also be required to save and verify an email address before they are able to send test email notifications. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://aka.ms/azureqa). If you have a support plan and need technical help, create a support request. (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-portal/supportability/how-to-create-azure-support-request)

description_problem: You're receiving this notification because you are associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure Monitor container insights. On 30 September 2026, we'll retire the ContainerLog table in Azure Monitor and you'll need to transition to the ContainerLogV2 table. The ContainerLogV2 table offers all the functionality of ContainerLog, plus: Compatibility with the basic logs pricing tier. Additional pod and container metadata for easier querying. Support for multiline log entries. Recommended action To ensure your alerts and dashboards continue to work as expected, transition (https://aka.ms/containerlogmigration) to ContainerLogV2 by 30 September 2026. Help and support If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A (https://aka.ms/ContainerLogQA). If you have a support plan and need technical help, open the Azure portal (https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/overview) and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.
recommended_actions: To ensure your alerts and dashboards continue to work as expected, transition (https://aka.ms/containerlogmigration) to ContainerLogV2 by 30 September 2026.
